records.name: Androgen receptor
records.tldr: The androgen receptor can bind androgen hormones and regulate gene activity. Receptor staining, an RNA subtype and dependence on the receptor are different findings.
records.summary:
The full-length androgen receptor is a hormone-binding protein that can regulate transcription. Its interactions with other proteins, receptor form and cellular setting affect its activity.

Receptor amount, location, transcription and growth dependence are different observations. Nuclear AR immunostaining reports protein in sampled cells; a luminal androgen receptor, or LAR, label is a versioned RNA-classifier result. TBCRC 032 correlative analyses found AR protein expression alone insufficient to identify AR-dependent tumors. Neither staining nor classifier membership alone proves patient benefit.

Full-length AR has distinct regions for transcriptional regulation, DNA binding and ligand binding. Androgens can change receptor interactions, nuclear localization and regulatory-DNA binding, with effects determined by partners, accessible DNA and receptor form. Tran's antiandrogen experiments in prostate models tested binding, nuclear movement and transcriptional effects separately. An RNA signal does not characterize a truncated protein or transfer those prostate results to breast-cancer treatment.

A fictional tumor with 20% AR-positive nuclei but a non-LAR RNA classification need not have a mistaken result. The assays measure different layers; compare antibody, scoring, tumor-cell content, preservation, sampling, normalization and classifier version. Twenty percent stained nuclei is not twenty percent of patients expected to respond. Dependence requires a controlled receptor perturbation with downstream and growth or survival measurements.

Lehmann 2016 refined TNBCtype from six classes to four tumor-specific classes after immune and stromal contributions explained the former immunomodulatory and mesenchymal stem-like signals. LAR does not mean estrogen-receptor-positive disease. TBCRC 032 was a defined phase Ib/II metastatic breast-cancer study of enzalutamide with or without taselisib, with phase II focused on AR-positive TNBC; its exploratory correlations do not turn an RNA subtype into a universal treatment rule or import a prostate indication.

records.name: Androgen receptor signalling
records.tldr: Androgen receptor signalling is prostate cancer's engine. Testosterone becomes DHT, binds the androgen receptor, and drives growth genes. Castration removes the fuel; newer pills block the receptor or the enzyme that makes fuel inside the tumour.
records.summary: Testicular testosterone (and adrenal precursors converted intratumourally via CYP17A1) is reduced to DHT by 5α-reductase and binds AR, which translocates to the nucleus and drives PSA, TMPRSS2-ERG, and proliferation genes. GnRH agonists/antagonists shut testicular production; abiraterone blocks CYP17A1; enzalutamide, apalutamide, darolutamide block AR. Castration resistance arises via AR amplification, ligand-binding mutations, splice variants (AR-V7 lacks the ligand domain), glucocorticoid receptor substitution, and lineage plasticity to neuroendocrine phenotype.

records.name: Androgen receptor pathway inhibitor (ARPI)
records.tldr: The newer prostate cancer hormone pills (abiraterone, enzalutamide, apalutamide, darolutamide) that block the androgen receptor or the last steps of androgen production, used on top of standard testosterone suppression.
records.summary: Abiraterone blocks CYP17 androgen synthesis (given with prednisone); enzalutamide, apalutamide and darolutamide are potent AR antagonists. Adding an ARPI to ADT extends survival in metastatic hormone-sensitive disease (LATITUDE, ARCHES, TITAN, ARASENS), in non-metastatic castration-resistant disease and in castration-resistant disease before or after docetaxel. Resistance arises via AR amplification, ligand-binding domain mutations, the AR-V7 splice variant and lineage plasticity to neuroendocrine disease; switching ARPIs after failure gives little benefit, so PSMA radioligands, PARP inhibitors and chemotherapy follow. Older antiandrogens (bicalutamide) are weaker first-generation drugs.

notes: An androgen receptor pathway inhibitor can act on hormone production or on the receptor itself. These are different interventions. Testosterone and dihydrotestosterone are androgen hormones; the full-length androgen receptor is a hormone-responsive transcription factor that helps regulate which DNA instructions are read into RNA. Bicalutamide and enzalutamide act at its ligand-binding region rather than removing the hormone supply. Blocking this receptor is also different from blocking the estrogen receptor. A receptor can be present while its partners, sequence, abundance or cellular setting change what an antagonist does.

Tran and colleagues studied RD162 and MDV3100, later called enzalutamide, in defined prostate-cancer systems. They measured receptor binding, movement into the nucleus, binding to regulatory DNA and interaction with coactivator proteins separately. The compounds reduced nuclear translocation and impaired DNA binding and coactivator recruitment in those systems. A change in one of these measurements is evidence about that step; it does not by itself establish a breast-cancer treatment effect.

Follow the signal through four locations: hormone supply, receptor binding inside a cell, nuclear regulation of DNA-to-RNA transcription and a receptor form with a missing binding region. Splicing assembles RNA from selected segments, so different messages can encode different receptor proteins. TBCRC 032 identified AR-V7 and AR-V12 transcripts lacking the ligand-binding domain in a small patient analysis. A drug aimed at that region and an intervention that lowers hormone supply therefore test different steps. Neither a receptor drawing nor a positive stain establishes growth dependence or benefit in breast cancer.

Traina and colleagues studied enzalutamide in a single-arm phase II trial of locally advanced or metastatic androgen-receptor-positive triple-negative breast cancer. The breast-optimised immunohistochemistry assay allowed enrolment with more than 0% nuclear staining. The evaluable subgroup additionally required at least 10% nuclear staining and a postbaseline assessment: 78 of 118 enrolled patients met that definition. The abstract reported clinical benefit at 16 weeks in 25% of all enrolled patients and 33% of that subgroup. The trial registry defines this endpoint as complete or partial response, or stable disease for at least 16 weeks. It is not the percentage with tumour shrinkage, and a single treatment arm does not measure a survival advantage over another treatment.

TBCRC 032 tested enzalutamide with the PI3K inhibitor taselisib. Its phase Ib portion included hormone-receptor-positive and triple-negative metastatic breast cancer; its randomised phase II portion was restricted to androgen-receptor-positive triple-negative disease. The exploratory RNA analyses suggested different responses by luminal androgen receptor subtype and receptor form. Protein staining alone was insufficient to identify receptor-dependent tumours. These observations do not validate an RNA subtype as a universal selection rule, substitute another PI3K drug for taselisib or establish postoperative benefit.

An androgen-receptor immunohistochemistry result reports nuclear protein staining in a specimen. Record the antibody, sampled tissue, scoring procedure, percentage of stained tumour nuclei and the threshold used. An RNA classifier instead compares gene-expression patterns; it does not measure how many receptors a drug occupies. Twenty percent stained nuclei is not a twenty percent probability that a patient responds. Receptor function, assay-defined expression and clinical benefit require different evidence, with the treated population, analysis denominator and time horizon stated.

In a model experiment, report the actual compound, concentration and exposure time alongside receptor engagement, downstream transcription, cell growth and death. Compare treated and control conditions and check whether the exposure used in a binding assay is the exposure used in the cellular test. These measurements connect an intervention to a possible mechanism; the result still needs disease-specific clinical evidence before it becomes a treatment-selection claim.

If a fictional report says a receptor-positive group had a 16-week clinical benefit rate of one third, first inspect the endpoint definition and analysis population. When qualifying stable disease is included, one third does not mean one third of tumours shrank. Ask which assay defined positivity, who enrolled, who entered the evaluable denominator and how long disease control had to last. The receptor supplies a mechanism hypothesis; expression supplies an assay result; benefit needs evidence for the particular drug, population and outcome.

records.name: Androgen receptor-positive triple-negative breast cancer
aka: Androgen receptor expression in breast cancer
records.tldr: Some triple-negative breast cancers show androgen receptor protein on a specified staining assay. That finding differs from an RNA subtype and does not by itself establish receptor dependence or benefit from an AR drug.
records.summary: Androgen receptor is scored by nuclear immunohistochemistry. Gucalp used more than 10 percent staining as positive; Traina enrolled staining above 0 percent and defined an evaluable group with at least 10 percent staining and a postbaseline assessment. Of 424 patients with ER- and PR-negative advanced breast cancer screened centrally, 12 percent were AR-positive by the 10 percent rule; bicalutamide 150 mg daily gave a six-month clinical benefit rate of 19 percent (complete or partial response or stable disease over six months) and median progression-free survival of 12 weeks, with no grade 4 or 5 treatment-related events (Gucalp 2013). Enzalutamide 160 mg daily in 118 patients with locally advanced or metastatic AR-positive triple-negative disease gave a 16-week clinical benefit rate of 25 percent overall and 33 percent in the 78 evaluable patients with 10 percent or more nuclear staining, median progression-free survival of 2.9 and 3.3 months and median overall survival of 12.7 and 17.6 months; fatigue was the only treatment-related grade 3 or higher event above 2 percent (Traina 2018). AR protein staining and the luminal androgen receptor (LAR) RNA subtype are different measurements. Lehmann's 2011 work identified LAR by gene expression and tested bicalutamide in representative cell-line models. In the 2016 retrospective neoadjuvant datasets, pathological complete response was 29 percent for LAR and 41 percent for basal-like 1; these figures describe those datasets and treatments. TBCRC 032 correlative analyses suggested that AR protein expression alone was insufficient to identify AR-dependent tumors. Neither antiandrogen is approved for breast cancer; the luminal androgen receptor subtype page sets out the biology and the trials with PI3K-pathway inhibitors.

records.name: Luminal androgen receptor (LAR) subtype
records.tldr: LAR is a research gene-expression pattern with luminal and androgen-related programmes. It is different from AR protein staining, and its name alone does not establish benefit from androgen blockade.
records.summary:
LAR is a research expression profile enriched for luminal and androgen-related programmes despite the receptor-defined TNBC context. It appears in the original six-group TNBCtype system and the four-profile TNBCtype-4 refinement. Different classifiers also use an LAR label; retain the actual method instead of assuming that shared names create identical groups.

The defining 2011 experiments found bicalutamide sensitivity in representative LAR cell lines. The 2016 retrospective pooled neoadjuvant analysis reported pathological complete response in 29 percent of LAR cases (95 percent confidence interval 17 to 41), versus 41 percent for BL1 (33 to 51) and 18 percent for BL2 (9 to 28). These are specified historical datasets and treatments, not universal response probabilities.

AR protein staining, an RNA LAR call and histological apocrine features are different measurements. Clinical antiandrogen studies using AR immunohistochemistry do not automatically establish benefit in a prospectively defined RNA-LAR population.

records.name: Cyclin-dependent kinase inhibitors
records.tldr: These drugs block selected enzymes that control cell division or gene reading. The enzyme, exposure and measured outcome matter; slower growth can mean a pause rather than cell death.
records.summary:
Cyclin-dependent kinase inhibitors affect selected enzymes involved in cell-cycle progression, transcription or both. The kinase, regulatory partners, compound profile and exposure determine which functions are being tested.

A change in substrate phosphorylation, an RNA signal, reversible growth arrest, cell death, marrow protection and a clinical cancer outcome require different measurements. Clinical evidence remains specific to the product, disease, regimen and endpoint.

notes: Cyclin-dependent kinases are enzymes that transfer phosphate groups to proteins. Cyclins are regulatory protein partners; different kinase-partner combinations help control cell division or transcription, the reading of DNA into RNA. The family resembles a workshop with several jobs rather than one engine. Naming a drug a CDK inhibitor does not identify the job it changes, and the same kinase can participate in connected processes.

CDK4 and CDK6 help phosphorylate retinoblastoma protein, or RB, near the G1-to-S transition toward DNA copying. Their usual arrest mechanism depends on a functional RB restraint on cell-cycle transcription; detecting RB protein alone does not establish an intact circuit, and loss of RB1 can remove that route. CDK2 works with cyclins E and A in progression around DNA replication. These are selected overlapping roles, not exclusive assignments for every cell state. Cyclin E abundance by itself does not select a particular CDK2 inhibitor.

CDK7 contributes to transcription initiation and also activates other CDKs. Larochelle and colleagues showed connected CDK7 and CDK9 functions in human cells: CDK7 helped establish and release promoter-proximal pausing, including activation of CDK9, while CDK9 supported productive RNA elongation. These jobs cannot be sealed into separate boxes. If a test reports a fall in a short-lived transcript after a transcription-directed intervention, that is an RNA-output observation to verify, not proof of the cell-cycle arrest associated with CDK4/6 inhibition. The exact transcript and its response need to be measured.

Selectivity depends on the compound and achieved exposure; one drug can inhibit several CDKs. Horiuchi and colleagues tested purvalanol A and dinaciclib in breast-cancer models with elevated MYC, and used individual kinase knockdown to investigate attribution. Their paper describes dinaciclib activity against CDK1, CDK2, CDK5 and CDK9 and reports cell-death effects after CDK1 depletion in the tested triple-negative lines. This preclinical result is not a rule for choosing a modern CDK4/6 or CDK2 drug from MYC expression. Engagement, cell-cycle change and cell death remain different observations.

NATALEE tested ribociclib with a nonsteroidal aromatase inhibitor against that endocrine treatment alone in hormone-receptor-positive, HER2-negative stage II or III early breast cancer. The 2024 report found improved invasive disease-free survival at its prespecified interim analysis. It studied a specified endocrine regimen and disease population, not triple-negative breast cancer or all drugs called CDK inhibitors.

Trilaciclib uses a different purpose and schedule: short exposure before chemotherapy can transiently arrest susceptible blood-forming stem and progenitor cells to reduce myelosuppression. TRACES studied Chinese patients with extensive-stage small-cell lung cancer, including an open safety part and a randomised placebo-controlled part. Duration of severe neutropenia in cycle one was the primary myeloprotection endpoint in the randomised part. Blood counts and days of severe neutropenia measure marrow effects. They are not tumour shrinkage, and this endpoint does not establish a survival benefit in another cancer.

For a CDK experiment, name the phosphorylated substrate, the cell-cycle or transcription measurement, compound, exposure, time and controls. DNA-synthesis labelling, the proportion of sampled cells in each phase, RNA output, cell counts and death measurements answer different questions. A percentage of cells in G1 is not a percentage of patients who benefit. RB staining records protein presence; functional arrest needs a working pathway, and clinical usefulness needs the outcome actually tested in the relevant population.

In a fictional culture that stops dividing during drug exposure and regrows after washout, the observed pattern supports reversible arrest. It does not establish selective killing or durable tumour control. Test attribution to the intended kinase, measure death and longer-term regrowth, and compare relevant control cells. A pause used to protect marrow and an intervention intended to control a tumour can involve related machinery while pursuing different outcomes.

records.name: Cell cycle
records.tldr: Cells preparing to divide pass through regulated stages for growth, DNA copying and chromosome separation. Some cells remain functional while outside that cycle.
records.summary: G1 prepares the cell, S copies DNA, and G2 precedes the mitotic phase. Mitosis separates nuclear chromosomes; cytokinesis separates cytoplasm into daughter cells. G0 describes a noncycling state, which need not mean death or loss of function. Cyclins, CDKs and checkpoints regulate transitions, and their alteration can contribute to cancer without making every checkpoint absent or guaranteeing error-free division. Cell-cycle checkpoints and immune checkpoints describe different biological processes.

notes: DNA-content measurements commonly group G0/G1 and G2/M because each pair shares a DNA-content range. Appropriate additional markers and doublet discrimination are needed: two cells can resemble one cell with more DNA.

A Ki-67-positive fraction or snapshot phase distribution is not a division rate or a population doubling time. Time-resolved proliferation and cell-loss measurements answer further questions. CDK4/6 inhibitors and spindle-directed drugs affect different parts of the cycle.

On a simplified relative-DNA scale, G1 is the reference amount, S lies between that amount and twice it, and G2 and M before cell separation are about twice it. A late-mitotic drawing can show two nuclei within one cell. This scale is neither a universal tumour ploidy nor a way to distinguish G0 from G1 or G2 from M. A G0 branch is optional; return to G1 depends on the cell and conditions. Neither a snapshot nor equally sized sectors establishes phase durations.

records.name: The cell-cycle engine (cyclins & CDKs)
records.tldr: Cell division runs on a clock made of cyclins and their kinases (CDKs), each pair firing in order: D-CDK4/6 to leave rest, E-CDK2 to start copying DNA, A-CDK2 to finish, B-CDK1 to divide. Cancers speed the clock; CDK inhibitors slow it.
records.summary: Mitogens induce cyclin D, which with CDK4/6 mono-phosphorylates RB; cyclin E-CDK2 completes RB hyperphosphorylation, releasing E2F and committing the cell at the restriction point (the point of no return). Cyclin A-CDK2 drives S phase, cyclin A/B-CDK1 drive G2 and mitosis, with CDK1 activation controlled by WEE1/PKMYT1 (inhibitory phosphorylation) and CDC25 phosphatases. CDK7 (CAK) activates all CDKs and also drives transcription. INK4 proteins (p16 from CDKN2A) inhibit CDK4/6; CIP/KIP (p21, p27) inhibit CDK2; APC/C and SCF ubiquitin ligases destroy cyclins in order. Cancer alterations: CCND1 amplification, CDK4 amplification (liposarcoma), CDKN2A deletion (very common, also removes ARF), CCNE1 amplification (ovarian, gastric, endocrine-resistant breast), RB1 loss (SCLC, TNBC, resistant prostate). CDK4/6 inhibitors need intact RB; CCNE1 amplification and RB1 loss are the escape routes and the rationale for CDK2 inhibitors and CDK4-selective atirmociclib.

records.name: EGFR
records.tldr: A growth receptor that is mutated in some lung cancers and overproduced in others; the first great success of targeted pills.
records.summary: EGFR activating mutations (exon 19 del, L858R) drive ~15% of Western and ~40-50% of East Asian NSCLC; osimertinib is standard first-line. EGFR is also an antibody target in colorectal and head-and-neck cancer (cetuximab, panitumumab) and a component of bispecifics (amivantamab, EGFR×MET; EGFR×HER3 ADCs). Resistance via C797S, MET amplification, and histologic transformation is the central problem.

notes: EGFR, also called HER1 or ERBB1, is a receptor tyrosine kinase. Ligand binding outside the cell can change receptor arrangement and the activity of phosphate-transfer machinery inside. Cetuximab binds the extracellular region, whereas an EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitor acts at the intracellular kinase. An antibody conjugate instead adds a cargo-delivery job to target recognition. Its mechanism and evidence need separate assessment, including any antibody-mediated immune effects. A schematic contact or cargo arrow is not a molecular map of receptor processing, and delivery to a recognised target does not by itself establish dependence on the receptor kinase.

EGFR can feed RAS-MAPK and PI3K-AKT signalling, but these networks receive other inputs too. A downstream signal therefore does not uniquely identify the receptor driving it. Compare the actual inhibitor: which receptors and variants it covers, whether binding is reversible and what exposure is achieved. Evidence for an extracellular antibody cannot simply be assigned to an intracellular kinase inhibitor, even when both treatments use the same target name.

Lynch and colleagues linked defined EGFR kinase-domain mutations to gefitinib responsiveness in non-small-cell lung cancer and tested the mutant proteins in cultured cells. They found mutations in eight of nine responsive cancers and none of seven nonresponsive cancers in the reported comparison. This was evidence about specific alterations in that disease and about their functional consequences, not a rule that abundant EGFR protein in another cancer predicts response.

TBCRC 001 studied cetuximab with carboplatin in metastatic triple-negative breast cancer. Among 16 patients with paired biopsies, the expression-based EGFR pathway analysis showed activation in 13 and inhibition after treatment in five. The regimen given together from the start produced a 17% response rate; 31% had a response or prolonged disease stabilisation. The latter outcome is broader than objective response. Receptor abundance, measured pathway suppression and clinical disease control cannot be substituted for each other.

BALI-1 compared cisplatin with or without cetuximab in metastatic triple-negative breast cancer. Its primary overall-response endpoint was not met: response was 20% versus 10%, with P = 0.11. Progression-free survival was a secondary endpoint, and the reported overall-survival difference was not statistically significant. These results do not establish a general EGFR-treatment rule or postoperative benefit. The later erratum added a funding acknowledgement rather than changing these efficacy results.

An EGFR report identifies the specimen, assay, variant if any and sampling time. Immunostaining measures protein amount and location; sequencing measures a DNA alteration; receptor or downstream phosphorylation measures a particular signalling state. A staining score, variant allele fraction and signal normalised to a control have different denominators and units. In model tests, state concentration and controls and distinguish engagement from growth dependence. An unspecified EGFR-high cutoff cannot select every EGFR-directed medicine.

In a fictional culture with strong EGFR staining, reduced receptor phosphorylation after treatment and continued growth, the stain and phosphoprotein result can both be correct. Growth may have other support, and attribution to the intended target still needs controlled perturbation and comparable exposure. This pattern does not establish sensitivity or patient benefit. Explain separately how much receptor was observed, what the exact alteration does and which product-specific mechanism and clinical outcome have been demonstrated.

A total-EGFR measurement does not specify recognition by an EGFR806 CAR. Subham’s study used an mAb806-derived binding region in a particular construct and examined TNBC brain-metastasis tissue, cell lines and mice. Its antibody-derived spacer was modified to reduce Fc-receptor recognition. Statements about tumour-restricted binding or normal-brain expression in the introduction draw on earlier work; they are not a substitute for testing the proposed finished receptor against relevant healthy cells. This preclinical result is not a clinical breast-cancer benefit or safety estimate.

Triple-negative breast cancer: EGFR is amplified or gained in 23% of basal-like tumours but rarely mutated (Cancer Genome Atlas 2012), high-level amplification 3 to 6% by cohort (cBioPortal); EGFR-directed antibodies failed unselected, and the receptor now matters as one arm of the EGFR-HER3 bispecific antibody-drug conjugate izalontamab brengitecan.

Colorectal cancer: a target without an alteration. Cetuximab and panitumumab work in RAS and BRAF wild-type, left-sided disease regardless of EGFR copy number or expression, and no EGFR test selects them; the biomarkers are negative ones (Karapetis 2008, Douillard 2013) plus primary tumour side (Arnold 2017). High-level EGFR amplification is 1 to 2% (cBioPortal) and epiregulin overexpression marks the distal, ligand-dependent tumours (Missiaglia 2014). Acquired resistance is read in plasma as emerging KRAS, NRAS, BRAF and EGFR ectodomain alterations, detectable months before imaging (Misale 2012, Diaz 2012).

Lung cancer: mutated in 12.4% of resected Western adenocarcinoma and 47.4% of East Asian adenocarcinoma, with 28.4% in never-smoker whole genomes (cBioPortal), the widest ancestry gap of any biomarker in solid-tumour oncology. The mutation classes differ: exon 19 deletions (about 14% of adenocarcinomas), L858R (about 11%), exon 20 insertions (about 2%) and the uncommon G719X, L861Q and S768I variants need drug-specific evidence. Response to every generation, or resistance to every inhibitor, does not follow from the class name. In July 2025, the FDA granted accelerated approval to sunvozertinib for adults with locally advanced or metastatic non-small-cell lung cancer with an EGFR exon 20 insertion detected by an FDA-approved test after progression on or after platinum-based chemotherapy. Resistance is read in the same gene: T790M in 63% of rebiopsies after a first-generation inhibitor (Yu 2013) and C797S in 22% after osimertinib, where the allelic phase with T790M decides whether a combination can cover it (Thress 2015, Oxnard 2018). Immunohistochemistry measures protein rather than identifying these DNA alterations.

records.name: Receptor tyrosine kinase activation
records.tldr: Receptor tyrosine kinases can relay signals from outside a cell through protein phosphorylation. Receptor amount, signalling, drug binding and growth dependence are different measurements.
records.summary:
EGFR, FGFR and FLT3 are examples of receptor tyrosine kinases. Their normal roles and activation arrangements differ across receptor families.

Receptor amount, phosphorylation, direct drug engagement, growth dependence and clinical benefit are separate observations. Lower receptor phosphorylation supports a biochemical effect under the assay conditions but can also reflect indirect regulation; it does not by itself prove direct binding. A controlled functional effect with independent specificity tests is needed before assigning receptor dependence.

Many RTKs have extracellular ligand-binding regions, membrane-spanning regions and intracellular tyrosine-kinase machinery. Families activate differently: Zhang demonstrated an asymmetric EGFR kinase-domain interaction, while Stauber examined an FGF1-FGFR2 extracellular complex with a proposed heparin-related assembly arrangement. Ligand, helper molecules, receptor member and context matter. A downstream phosphosite can have multiple upstream causes and is not a universal receptor meter.

Slamon 1987 studied 189 primary breast cancers and reported HER2 amplification in 30%, associated with relapse and survival; that historical study is not a present-day universal prevalence or a causal drug-response experiment. In the 2001 randomized trial of 469 women with HER2-overexpressing metastatic breast cancer, adding trastuzumab to chemotherapy increased median survival from 20.3 to 25.1 months, with cardiac toxicity as a material risk. A trial median summarizes a group and does not predict an individual survival time.

In a fictional comparison, two cultures contain a receptor, but only the amplified, high-surface-protein culture slows growth after a blocking antibody, while receptor phosphorylation falls in both. This separates amount, sampled signaling and growth response; the pattern suggests dependence but attribution still needs controls and independent perturbation. RNA is not surface accessibility, a family-name inhibitor need not engage every member at the tested exposure. For an antibody-drug conjugate, receptor access and payload delivery are separate questions from whether growth requires that receptor's signaling. Fixed-tissue staining and viable-model perturbation have different input costs and validation scopes.

records.tldr: PARP inhibitors block DNA repair. Some cancers with defective repair are especially vulnerable, but the gene, disease setting and treatment combination determine which evidence applies.
records.summary: PARP1 and PARP2 are distinct DNA-repair enzymes. This page covers drugs that inhibit one or both; the molecular structures and identifiers shown here refer to PARP1. Approved PARP1/2 inhibitors exploit repair dependency, while selective PARP1 programmes seek a wider therapeutic window. Biomarker selection varies by country, drug and disease: US breast labels for olaparib and talazoparib require germline BRCA alterations; somatic BRCA breast activity is supported by metastatic phase 2 evidence rather than an adjuvant approval. Genomic HRD scars, current functional repair and individual HRR genes are not interchangeable. In TBCRC 048, ATM or CHEK2 alterations alone did not produce responses; the 2026 expansion found activity in germline PALB2 and somatic BRCA cohorts, but the somatic cohort missed its prespecified response target. PARP inhibitors can cause substantial marrow toxicity. GS-0201 plus sacituzumab govitecan and palacaparib plus datopotamab deruxtecan connect repair dependency with antibody-directed delivery in early trials.

records.tldr: These medicines disrupt DNA repair processes. Some also retain repair proteins on DNA; a repair-gene finding alone does not establish that they will help.
records.summary: PARP inhibitors reduce PARP enzyme activity and can stabilise PARP complexes on damaged DNA. Catalytic output, DNA-associated occupancy, repair capacity and cell survival are different measurements. Experimental sensitivity depends on the current cellular repair state, and repair-restoring changes can contribute to resistance. Clinical eligibility depends on the particular medicine, cancer setting, previous treatment and required companion test; a shared mechanism is not a shared indication.

notes: PARP means poly(ADP-ribose) polymerase, a protein family involved in cellular signalling and repair. PARP1 is one representative. At damaged DNA it can build signals on proteins from chains of the chemical unit ADP-ribose, called poly(ADP-ribose), or PAR. Catalytic inhibition reduces this output. Some inhibitors can also stabilise DNA-associated PARP complexes, often called trapping. A repair-worker analogy separates a reduced call for help from a worker remaining in a doorway; proteins and medicines have no purpose, and the cell has more than one response route.

Murai 2012 compared niraparib, olaparib and veliparib in defined cellular and biochemical systems: niraparib and olaparib trapped PARP-DNA complexes more strongly than veliparib, despite catalytic inhibition being a different comparison. Murai 2014 compared BMN673, now talazoparib, with olaparib and rucaparib. In damaged-DNA cell assays, 0.1 micromolar BMN673 produced a trapping signal comparable to 10 micromolar olaparib, about a 100-fold concentration difference; the purified DNA-binding assay gave a different, roughly 40-fold comparison. Similar catalytic effects did not imply similar trapping. Strongest among compounds tested in 2014 is not a ranking of clinical benefit, tolerated exposure or personal treatment choices.

A DNA-associated protein obstacle can challenge copying without every encounter becoming a measured collision, double-strand break or cell death. Farmer 2005 demonstrated increased sensitivity to PARP inhibition in experimental BRCA-deficient systems. Cong 2021 studied single-stranded replication gaps in cellular models: gap suppression tracked resistance or resensitisation, while restoring fork protection did not always restore resistance in the tested models. Obstacle and gap explanations can coexist, but their relative contribution in a patient's tumour is not established by these experiments. A repair-gene variant alone does not reproduce the functional losses tested in a synthetic-lethal experiment.

Two schematic pictures ask different questions. Matched snapshots of DNA-bound PARP1 with a longer or shorter PAR chain illustrate catalytic output; a generic inhibitor in the catalytic pocket does not measure binding duration. A second picture places approaching copying machinery behind a retained PARP1 complex, with visible separation; it does not show an observed collision, literal backbone conformation or a measured effect size. Reduced catalytic activity and DNA retention can occur together. The arrows therefore lead to further context-dependent measurements, rather than two independent proofs of a clinical mechanism or a drug ranking.

Enzyme assays and PAR immunoassays report catalytic activity or its product. NCI's PAR assay measures PAR levels in specified biospecimens; chromatin-associated PARP measurements instead investigate DNA retention under specified conditions. Repair readouts and survival/regrowth experiments add other information. Murai's experiments used defined cell lines, DNA damage and drug concentrations, so neither a reduced metabolic or ATP signal alone nor a picture establishes irreversible death or its cause. Matched genetic perturbations and appropriate controls are needed to distinguish reduced growth, reduced metabolism and loss of long-term survival.

Waks's selected resistant breast cancer cohort illustrates why historical repair markers and current repair can diverge: four definite or putative BRCA reversion cases acquired RAD51 foci, and other proposed routes included 53BP1 loss and MRE11A amplification. The 53BP1-loss case lacked enough tissue for direct functional confirmation. A historical scar or sequence hypothesis cannot establish a present PARP vulnerability, and this small cohort does not supply an all-patient resistance rule. Biological plausibility, a qualifying label indication and a trial place are separate requirements.

For example, the U.S. olaparib label effective July 2025 specifies adjuvant treatment of adults with deleterious or suspected-deleterious germline BRCA-mutated, HER2-negative high-risk early breast cancer after neoadjuvant or adjuvant chemotherapy, selected with an approved companion diagnostic. A tumour-only BRCA result or high scar score cannot replace the germline and disease-setting requirements. That indication does not establish that a different PARP inhibitor, a different setting or a plausible mechanism has the same approval or access conditions.

In a fictional comparison, compounds A and B inhibit PARP catalytic activity similarly, but A retains more PARP on DNA in a culture assay. The conclusion is an assay-specific trapping difference. Useful exposure, survival, safety, resistance and clinical outcomes still need evidence. More trapping in that system does not establish a better treatment, and neither an old scar nor a repair-gene name identifies which effect matters in the current tumour.

Hoslett and colleagues' 2026 preclinical study investigated selective disposal of trapped PARP1 involving TEX264, the protein-remodelling enzyme p97 and LC3-associated lysosomal handling. Autophagic handling of nuclear material is called nucleophagy. Perturbing the machinery increased chromatin-associated PARP1 and PARP-inhibitor sensitivity in the studied systems; complementation and cargo-recognition experiments supported the proposed route. Some trapping experiments also supplied the DNA-damaging agent MMS, so their conditions are not every drug-alone exposure. The authors left the exact export or packaging of nuclear cargo, and macroautophagy versus direct microautophagy, unresolved. A clearance cartoon is therefore a mechanistic model, not established compartment geometry. Expression-survival associations do not validate TEX264 expression as a treatment-response test.

In a fictional culture, more death with a PARP inhibitor plus a lysosomal drug fits several explanations: reduced clearance of trapped PARP, toxicity from the second drug itself, or another altered stress response. Measure chromatin-bound PARP1 over the relevant interval, include both single-drug conditions, and test the proposed clearance machinery with suitable independent perturbation and restoration. Unchanged trapped cargo despite more death argues against that particular clearance explanation. TEX264 or p97 perturbation is complementary evidence, not automatically perfectly selective, because proteins can have other functions. Chloroquine and hydroxychloroquine alter lysosomal processes broadly. Survival alone, high recycling RNA or a broad lysosomal effect does not identify selective trapped-PARP disposal or establish patient benefit.

records.name: DNA damage response & homologous recombination
records.tldr: Cells detect DNA damage, coordinate repair and adjust their cell cycle. A damage signal is different from completed repair, and a repair-gene finding alone does not predict treatment benefit.
records.summary:
A DNA lesion is a physical or chemical problem; a mutation is a lasting sequence change. Repair can remove damage before a mutation is fixed. Recognition and checkpoint signaling are responses to the problem, whereas successful repair, tolerated damage, arrest and death are separate outcomes. The lesson map therefore ends by measuring the outcome instead of assuming that the alarm completed the repair.

Selected repair jobs address different problems: base excision begins by removing a damaged base, nucleotide excision removes a lesion-containing stretch, and mismatch repair corrects copying mismatches. Lindahl purified an E. coli enzyme that released uracil without cutting the DNA backbone, a specific early base-excision step rather than proof of all human repair routes. Double-strand breaks can use matching-template homologous repair or end joining. These are selected jobs, not exclusive assignments of every lesion to one pathway.

Gamma-H2AX is histone H2AX phosphorylated at serine 139. Rogakou 1998 observed a rapid response after experimentally induced double-strand breaks in mammalian systems. A microscopy focus is a response around damage, not direct sequencing of a break or a universal repair-failure test. In a fictional culture with a bulky lesion and increased gamma-H2AX, measure lesion removal over time with suitable controls before claiming nucleotide-excision failure, homologous repair deficiency or drug sensitivity.

Platinum agents can form DNA crosslinks; interstrand links block strand separation and require coordinated repair machinery. The Fanconi pathway links DNA-processing activities, and homologous repair can contribute to resolving replication-associated damage. This does not mean every platinum lesion is an interstrand link or that every HR-deficient tumor responds. A repair mechanism, an observed drug effect and clinical benefit in a defined population need separate evidence.

records.name: ATR
records.tldr: ATR is a DNA-damage alarm kinase. Blocking it makes tumours with broken repair systems collapse under their own replication stress.
records.summary: ATR is a PI3K-like kinase activated by single-stranded DNA at stalled replication forks; it signals through CHK1 to pause the cell cycle and stabilise forks. Tumours with ATM loss, high replication stress or PARP-inhibitor resistance depend on this alarm, so blocking ATR can make them collapse under their own replication stress. ATR inhibitors (ceralasertib, camonsertib, elimusertib) are in phase 2 and 3, notably ceralasertib with durvalumab in NSCLC after immunotherapy (LATIFY) and in ATM-deficient tumours; ATM loss or mutation is found in about 5 to 10 percent of lung adenocarcinomas. No approval has yet been granted, and myelosuppression limits how freely ATR inhibitors can be combined with chemotherapy or PARP inhibitors. Defining a predictive biomarker beyond ATM loss is the key open problem. For a newcomer: ATR is a DNA-damage alarm that broken-repair tumours cannot afford to lose.

records.name: WEE1
records.tldr: A checkpoint kinase that gives cells time to fix DNA before dividing. Removing it forces damaged cancer cells into a fatal division.
records.summary: WEE1 is a checkpoint kinase that inhibits CDK1 to enforce the G2/M checkpoint, giving cells time to repair DNA before dividing. TP53-mutant cells have lost their G1 checkpoint and depend on WEE1 to avoid entering mitosis with damaged DNA, so inhibiting it forces them into a lethal division. Adavosertib showed activity in uterine serous carcinoma and other TP53-mutant tumours, but its development was paused; azenosertib (ZN-c3) and Debio 0123 continue in ovarian and other cancers. The strongest rationale is in CCNE1-amplified disease, seen in 15 to 20 percent of ovarian cancers, where TP53 mutation is also near-universal. Haematological and gastrointestinal toxicity have limited dosing, and no WEE1 inhibitor is yet approved. In plain terms, removing this checkpoint pushes damaged cancer cells into a division they cannot survive.

records.name: PI3K / AKT / mTOR
records.tldr: This network links growth signals and nutrients to protein production, metabolism and recycling. Different branches can respond differently to an intervention.
records.summary:
Class I PI3K phosphorylates a membrane lipid, producing PIP3; PTEN removes its position-3 phosphate. AKT and mTOR are protein kinases. A PIP3 lipid result and an AKT1 Ser473 phosphosite result are therefore different molecular measurements. Document specimen preservation, cell mixture, protein site, timing, exposure, comparator and total-protein normalization before interpreting a change as activity or dependence.

Membrane recruitment helps organize AKT activation. PDK1 phosphorylates AKT1 Thr308, whereas the rictor-mTOR complex supplies Ser473 phosphorylation in the defined experimental route. AKT can inhibit TSC2, relieving the TSC1/2 brake on RHEB, which promotes mTORC1 signaling. The diagram's indirect AKT-to-mTORC1 connection stands for these regulatory steps; it is not direct phosphorylation of mTORC1 by AKT.

Raptor-containing mTORC1 and rictor-containing mTORC2 are distinct complexes. mTORC1 regulates protein production and autophagy-initiation machinery; releasing initiation restraint is not proof of completed recycling flux. Harrington linked S6K activity to reduced IRS-1 function, and O'Reilly observed increased IRS-1 and AKT signaling after RAD001 in cell models and treated tumors. Feedback release can change an output without proving that a combination improves outcomes in every setting.

In a fictional mTORC1 perturbation, lower production-regulator phosphorylation followed by higher AKT1 Ser473 and unchanged growth supports biochemical changes, not essentiality or failed engagement; timing alone does not prove the feedback connection. Test the proposed wiring and functional outcome independently. The FDA's 2023 capivasertib-with-fulvestrant approval specified adults with hormone-receptor-positive, HER2-negative advanced breast cancer, qualifying PIK3CA/AKT1/PTEN alterations on an approved test and specified prior endocrine treatment or early recurrence. It is not a TNBC indication inferred from a pathway label.

notes: PI3K means phosphoinositide 3-kinase; AKT is also called protein kinase B. Mechanistic target of rapamycin complex 1, mTORC1, integrates growth and nutrient inputs. PTEN, phosphatase and tensin homolog, removes a phosphate from a PI3K-generated lipid signal. These protein and lipid reactions need their own readouts. Ibrahim 2012 found that PI3K inhibition reduced BRCA1/2 expression and increased PARP-inhibitor sensitivity in the BRCA-proficient triple-negative breast cancer models studied. A second branch concerns mTORC1 restraint of ULK1-associated autophagy initiation, studied by Kim 2011. Releasing an initiation brake does not establish completed cargo degradation or protective recycling. The two branches can change together without revealing the net survival effect. A model already lacking the relevant repair function cannot be assumed to gain the same vulnerability as one in which that function is newly reduced; measure protein and repair function, flux and survival under the actual compound, dose and schedule.

Rapalogs, PI3K or AKT inhibitors and ATP-site mTOR kinase inhibitors are different interventions. In Rodrik-Outmezguine's 2011 models, inhibiting both mTOR complexes initially reduced AKT Ser473 and Thr308 phosphorylation, but relief of receptor feedback later restored Thr308 phosphorylation and AKT signalling while Ser473 remained suppressed. A Ser473 result therefore did not measure all AKT activity. O'Reilly's rapalog study and Harrington's IRS feedback work likewise explain why lower mTORC1 output can coexist with increased upstream signalling. These are measured responses in specified systems, not inevitable behaviour or a universal combination prescription.

In a fictional experiment, repair RNA falls, an mTORC1-associated phosphosite falls, AKT phosphorylation rises and more autophagosomes appear. The RNA concerns messages; confirm the proposed protein and repair consequence. A validated site change concerns that output at that time, while the AKT change may fit feedback without proving every downstream effect. Autophagosome amount does not establish completed flux, and no survival conclusion has yet been supplied. Growth and energy inputs also differ: Gwinn 2008 linked AMPK phosphorylation of raptor to mTORC1 restraint during energy stress. Slower costly building work and better survival can coexist. Named S6, 4E-BP1, AKT and AMPK-target sites need their own controls, total-protein context and timing; bulk RNA is not a kinase-activity meter.

PIK3CA encodes the PI3K-alpha catalytic subunit. PIKFYVE is a different lipid kinase involved in endolysosomal regulation. Similar names do not make them the same target, and evidence about one does not automatically describe the other.

notes: PI3K, AKT and mTOR name different parts of a signalling network. In the selected membrane route, PI3K adds a phosphate to the lipid PIP2 to make PIP3; PTEN removes the relevant phosphate and opposes that lipid signal. PIP3 helps recruit proteins including AKT to the membrane. AKT, also called protein kinase B, phosphorylates proteins, and its connection to mTORC1 includes intermediate regulators. mTOR participates in the distinct mTORC1 and mTORC2 complexes. A diagram showing this route leaves other branches out.

Alpelisib has inhibitory activity predominantly against PI3K-alpha; capivasertib inhibits AKT isoforms; the rapamycin derivative everolimus acts through a complex that inhibits mTOR. Isoforms are related forms of a protein, and an inhibitor profile must identify which forms or complexes the compound affects. Binding mode, selectivity and achieved exposure differ between products. Blocking a neighbouring node is not the same intervention, even when the network diagram puts the names beside each other.

O'Reilly and colleagues found that mTOR inhibition relieved feedback inhibition and increased AKT activation in studied cancer cell lines and patient tumour samples. The indirect return path in a network sketch represents a feedback brake, not a direct physical wire or every branch. In a fictional experiment, reduced downstream output with a higher AKT phosphosite signal is compatible with network compensation. Those two measurements alone do not prove that this loop caused the change, that every tumour rebounds or that the drug missed its target; they also do not measure net survival benefit.

The FDA's November 2023 capivasertib approval is a defined historical example: capivasertib with fulvestrant for adults with hormone-receptor-positive, HER2-negative locally advanced or metastatic breast cancer carrying a PIK3CA, AKT1 or PTEN alteration detected by an FDA-approved test. It required progression after an endocrine-based regimen in the metastatic setting, or recurrence on or within 12 months of completing adjuvant therapy. These disease, test, combination and prior-treatment conditions do not become a triple-negative breast-cancer indication from a pathway alteration alone.

CAPItello-290 tested capivasertib plus paclitaxel against placebo plus paclitaxel as first-line treatment for metastatic triple-negative breast cancer. In the 812-patient phase III trial, the overall-survival primary endpoints were not met in either the overall population or the PIK3CA/AKT1/PTEN-altered population. Median overall survival was 17.7 versus 18.0 months overall and 20.4 months in both altered-population arms. Secondary progression-free survival results favoured the combination, but do not reverse the negative primary survival finding.

Name the phosphosite, substrate, specimen, comparator and time when interpreting a signalling assay. A PTEN DNA alteration, RNA amount, protein stain and enzyme-function result measure different layers. A drug-dependent change in AKT phosphorylation is not a universal meter of all AKT activity; examine the relevant substrate effects too. Nanomolar, or nM, states concentration; normalised phosphoprotein signal, growth and death are distinct outputs. Engagement is different from dependence, and clinical interpretation needs the disease, assay and endpoint used in the treatment evidence.

If a fictional report finds a PIK3CA variant, it does not follow that any AKT inhibitor will work. Establish the variant's functional effect, actual drug and exposure, disease setting, assay and clinical evidence before claiming sensitivity or eligibility. Likewise, a model hypothesis about DNA repair or immune effects is not proof that every PI3K or AKT inhibitor improves a PARP-inhibitor or immunotherapy combination. State the proposed mechanism, the particular node being perturbed and the outcome tested in that treatment setting.

records.summary: AKT1, AKT2 and AKT3 are serine/threonine kinases at the centre of the PI3K survival pathway, and the AKT1 E17K hotspot is an activating mutation found in about 3 to 5 percent of hormone-receptor-positive breast cancers. Capivasertib (Truqap), a pan-AKT inhibitor, is approved with fulvestrant in HR-positive breast cancer carrying PIK3CA, AKT1 or PTEN alterations (CAPItello-291), a group that makes up around half of such tumours, and from 2026 with abiraterone in PTEN-deficient metastatic prostate cancer (CAPItello-281). PTEN loss activates the pathway in roughly 15 to 20 percent of prostate cancers and around 40 percent of metastatic castration-resistant disease. Hyperglycaemia, diarrhoea and rash are the class toxicities, and whether unselected patients also benefit is contested. In plain terms, AKT is the survival kinase downstream of PI3K, now blocked in breast and prostate cancer.

notes: DNA is the cell's genetic material. During copying, a replication fork can slow or stall; that stress is not itself a diagnosis of a double-strand break. A workshop analogy separates pausing the job, stabilising unfinished work and repairing damage, while the actual response is an overlapping network. UniProt describes ATM-associated signalling after double-strand breaks and ATR-associated checkpoint signalling during replication stalling; ATR can phosphorylate CHK1 and other substrates. These labels do not make two proteins the only sensors or reduce each to one job.

A kinase transfers a phosphate group to a substrate; phosphorylation does not always turn that substrate on. WEE1 phosphorylates CDK1 at tyrosine 15 and inhibits entry into mitosis. CHK1 also acts through checkpoint and repair pathways, including inhibition of CDC25 regulators. A simplified p53/G1 and WEE1/G2 checkpoint drawing can motivate a hypothesis after defined functional checkpoint loss; a TP53 sequence variant alone does not prove that the first pause is absent or that a second pause is a validated treatment dependency. Hirai 2009 tested WEE1 inhibition with DNA-damaging drugs in specified p53-deficient models, not a universal clinical TP53-selection rule.

Reaper 2011 reported an ATR-inhibitor interaction with ATM-p53 pathway deficiency in cells treated with DNA-damaging agents. That experimental context matters: an ATM alteration is not automatically functional loss, and this result is not an all-tumour monotherapy rule. Gatti-Mays 2020 studied prexasertib in nine people with previously treated recurrent or metastatic triple-negative breast cancer who were germline-BRCA wild-type. One had a partial response, four had stable disease, and eight had grade 3 or 4 afebrile neutropenia. This small single-group pilot illustrates both activity and marrow toxicity at its tested exposure; it does not validate a general repair-variant biomarker or a routine combination schedule.

DNA-PK's catalytic component, PRKDC, participates in classical non-homologous end joining with other end-binding and repair proteins. Polymerase theta, encoded by POLQ, supports a different end-joining route that can use short sequence matches. Blocking checkpoint signalling and blocking an end-joining route are different interventions even if each reduces survival in a model. A rationale for combining a DNA-PK inhibitor with DNA damage or radiation does not by itself establish selective tumour benefit or spare normal dividing tissue. Synthetic lethality requires evidence about the paired functional defects, rather than two gene names on a report.

Zatreanu 2021 studied ART558, an allosteric inhibitor of polymerase theta's polymerase domain. It impaired theta-mediated end joining rather than classical non-homologous end joining, and showed activity in selected BRCA-deficient models, including PARP-resistant models with 53BP1 or Shieldin loss. Zhou 2021 instead studied novobiocin against the ATPase domain in cell and mouse tumour models. These are different compounds and domains; their experimental specificity and activity cannot be transferred automatically to another polymerase-theta drug or to a patient.

The novobiocin study also tested BRCA2-reverted PEO4 and CAPAN1-CR cells against their deficient parental lines. The reverted cells resisted both PARP inhibition and novobiocin. Other PARP-resistant models, including a BRCA1-mutant/53BP1-loss model, remained novobiocin-sensitive. Thus PARP resistance alone did not identify one common vulnerability, and the study does not establish resistance to every polymerase-theta inhibitor. In two fictional PARP-resistant cultures, one retaining a BRCA defect with 53BP1 loss and another carrying a BRCA2 reversion, test the actual compound and current repair state separately. Even a positive experiment leaves clinical benefit and safety unresolved.

The measurement question determines the assay. Engagement and downstream action can be investigated with specified phosphorylation sites, such as WEE1-related CDK1 tyrosine 15, rather than an unspecified phosphate signal. DNA-damage markers, RAD51 or other repair foci, functional repair assays, and survival or regrowth after drug removal ask further questions. Foci are visible protein clusters, not proof by themselves that repair finished successfully. Use matched repair-proficient and deficient models, genetic controls, specified concentrations, exposure times and sampling times. Nanomolar means nanomoles per litre and micromolar means micromoles per litre; a culture concentration is not a clinical dose.

A three-panel teaching cartoon can show an ATR-associated stress signal, WEE1 placing an inhibitory phosphate, and polymerase-theta joining with short matches. Its bars and DNA strokes supply schematic roles, not concentrations, a complete literal network or a treatment ranking. Follow a checkpoint diagram by asking what functional loss is demonstrated, what job is interrupted and what measured dependency remains. A historical genomic scar does not establish the current repair state; a PARP-resistant label does not establish polymerase-theta sensitivity; and loss of one checkpoint does not establish clinical benefit from inhibiting another. These distinctions also prevent treating ATR inhibition and an ATM-loss biomarker as the same fact.
